# Outreach vs Salesloft (2026): What Everyone Gets Wrong

Outreach built Deal Agent. Salesloft merged with Clari. Here's what each platform shipped and what both still miss. September 2026.

### **TL;DR**

Outreach and Salesloft are still compared as if they're fighting over the same thing: which sales engagement platform helps reps send better sequences. But both platforms have moved beyond.

Outreach spent H1 2026 building toward a platform that acts on deals for reps. Salesloft spent the first half of 2026 becoming a forecasting and revenue orchestration company that still does engagement.

Neither of them however, _and this is the part nobody's saying_, has anything to say about what happens before a rep ever opens a sequence.

That's the gap we built [Breakout](https://getbreakout.ai/) for.

### **Outreach vs Salesloft, By the Numbers**

Here's what the numbers actually say if you're building a shortlist today.

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Outreach** | **Salesloft** |
| **List price** | ~$100–160/user/month across Amplify Core, Plus, and Pro, quote-based, billed annually ( [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/outreach)) | ~$125–165/user/month across Essentials, Advanced, and Premier, quote-based, 10–15 seat minimum ( [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/salesloft)) |
| **Hidden costs** | Implementation fees of $5,000–25,000+, platform fees of $2,000–5,000/year | Dialer and Conversation Intelligence priced as separate add-ons, 8–12% annual price escalators standard on multi-year terms |
| **G2 rating** | 4.3 out of 5 across 3,500+ reviews ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/compare/outreach-vs-selling-com)) | 4.5 out of 5 across 4,200+ reviews ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/compare/connectandsell-vs-salesloft)) |
| **Typical time to full adoption** | 2–3 months, reps report a steep learning curve | 2–4 weeks, consistently the stronger score on ease of setup and admin |
| **Where 2026 R&D actually went** | Deal Agent: autonomous field updates, AI-recommended deal actions applied without rep sign-off | Conversation Intelligence: call and buyer-signal data feeding Clari's forecast engine in real time |

Most people comparing these two platforms have read some version of the same nine paragraphs a dozen times: Outreach is the enterprise pick with deeper reporting and a steeper learning curve, Salesloft is faster to roll out with a cleaner UI, pick based on team size and budget. Every word of that used to be true. It's also increasingly beside the point.

Salesloft's higher G2 score isn't a fluke, and it isn't new either. Reps have consistently rated it easier to use for years. But that edge comes specifically from setup and admin, not from having more features than Outreach.

Outreach, on the other hand, costs more to implement because it provides deeper conditional logic and finer admin control; the real reason it keeps winning deals with 50+ teams with a dedicated RevOps function.

None of that changed in 2026. What did change is how much of the AI in both platforms now acts on its own.

That's not really an Outreach or Salesloft story; it's an industry-wide one. Gartner expects 40% of enterprise software to include task-specific AI agents by the end of this year, up from under 5% in 2025. Sales tools are moving even faster than that average. SDR-focused AI agents are paying back their cost in a median of 3.4 months, per BCG and Forrester's 2026 research. Both Outreach and Salesloft have built their 2026 roadmaps into that shift, just aimed at different problems.

For Outreach, that pivot meant Deal Agent — a software that doesn't just flag a stalled deal, but updates the record and recommends the next move without a rep opening the tab.

Salesloft took a different route to the same shift. Its core strength was always engagement and sequencing, not agentic deal execution, where Outreach already had a head start. Rather than race to catch up on Outreach's turf, Salesloft leaned into what it already had: years of call and engagement data.

A December 2025 merger with Clari, a company already built around forecasting, gave that data somewhere new to go, right as missed revenue forecasts became an expensive, board-level problem at a lot of companies. (The actual numbers on that are below.) Where Outreach's 2026 work went into an agent that acts inside a deal, Salesloft's went into feeding its engagement data into Clari's forecasting engine.

### **What Outreach Actually Shipped in 2026**

Outreach is building toward reps managing deals through an AI layer that acts, not a sequence tool that reminds you to follow up. That's a genuine shift in ambition. It's also a shift that assumes a rep already has a deal in front of them.

- **February:** Deal Agent launches, recommending fixes to deals in flight

- **Later release:** Deal Agent starts applying those fixes without a rep clicking anything

- **July:** Deal Agent can now write directly into picklist, numeric, and percentage fields, so it can update a close probability or a lost reason on its own

- **Ongoing:** Omni lets reps pull answers and pipeline actions from a single conversational interface instead of digging through tabs


### **What Salesloft Actually Became in 2026**

[52% of CFOs at U.S. middle-market firms](https://www.pymnts.com/study_posts/how-middle-market-business-uncertainty-rewrote-2025/) said their companies fell short of their 2025 performance goals, according to PYMNTS Intelligence. That's the kind of number the Clari-Salesloft merger is actually trying to fix, and it's a real, expensive problem worth solving.

- **December 2025:** The Clari merger closes, combining Clari's forecasting with Salesloft's engagement platform under CEO Steve Cox

- **Spring 2026:** The two platforms unify further and introduce a Model Context Protocol server, opening live revenue data to third-party AI tools

- **July 2026:** Salesloft Conversation Intelligence launches, meaning call data no longer sits in a coaching dashboard, it feeds a live signal layer that sharpens the forecast in real time

- **Ongoing:** Gartner's first Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration names Clari a Leader and Salesloft a Visionary, inside the same combined entity


This means that Salesloft, the engagement platform reps used to compare feature-for-feature against Outreach, is now a smaller piece of a bigger forecasting story. Independent analysts covering the merger have flagged the same caution to buyers. Seven months in, the platform is still running on separate interfaces with no unified roadmap published, a fact worth knowing if your renewal is coming up in the next two quarters.

### **The Question That Is Skipped Entirely**

Zoom out and both roadmaps answer the same underlying question: what do we do once a rep has a lead and a deal to work?

Outreach wants to execute that deal for you. Salesloft, now Clari, wants to forecast it more accurately. Genuinely useful problems, both of them. But they start at the same place, after someone already has a name, a company, and a reason to reach out.

> That starting point used to have an answer. Drift built its entire business on catching a visitor while they were still on your website, before a rep or a sequence ever got involved. Salesloft acquired Drift, then sunset it in March 2026 and pointed customers toward 1mind, an AI avatar built to run entire sales motions autonomously.
>
> Whatever the merits of that hand-off, it means the tool that used to sit upstream of both Outreach and Salesloft, catching intent before it became a lead, isn't part of either platform's story anymore.

So the honest answer isn't which one between Outreach and Salesloft "wins". It's that a VP evaluating engagement tools this year has two strong options for what happens after someone's already in the pipeline, and close to nothing from either vendor for the twenty minutes before that, when a real buyer is on your pricing page right now deciding whether to fill out a form or close the tab.

### **Where This Actually Leaves You**

- **Pick Outreach** if reps not executing consistently on deals they already have is your bottleneck, and you can absorb the steeper onboarding and higher implementation cost

- **Pick Salesloft** if forecast accuracy matters more than engagement polish, and you're comfortable being an early customer on a still-integrating platform, confirm renewal terms and roadmap commitments before signing given the ongoing merger work

- **Neither one solves** what happens before a lead exists in the first place


Both Outreach and Salesloft are legitimate choices for outbound execution, and this piece isn't here to talk you out of either one.

> If website visitors are showing real intent today and nobody's talking to them until a rep manually notices and adds them to a sequence, that gap doesn't close no matter which of these two platforms you pick.

### **That's the part of the funnel we built Breakout to own.**

[Breakout](https://getbreakout.ai/) doesn't just identify anonymous visitors or surface buying signals. It handles the entire inbound workflow. With Breakout, you can:

- **Identify** anonymous visitors at the company and person level the moment they land on your site, no form fill required. Breakout builds a full buyer profile from reverse-IP data, UTM source, firmographic fit, and the specific page someone's on, so you know who's there before they ever raise a hand.

- **Engage** them in an actual AI-led conversation, not a rules-based chatbot decision tree. The AI holds context across the conversation, answers real product questions, and adapts based on what that visitor does next, instead of routing them through a fixed script.

- **Show, not just tell**, surfacing the right case study, demo, or pricing view based on what that visitor is actually doing on your site. A repeat visitor who's spent time on your pricing page sees a different next step than someone on their first visit to your docs.

- **Follow up automatically** across email and LinkedIn if a high-intent visitor bounces before converting, using the same session context Breakout captured while they were on-site, so the follow-up isn't a cold restart.

- **Hand your reps a qualified meeting**, not a name to guess at. Most teams are live within three hours of setup, with no engineering lift and no Salesforce dependency required to get started.

| **Typical setup time** | 2–3 months | 2–4 weeks | Under 3 hours |
| **Requires Salesforce** | No | No | No |

Within weeks, we increased our meetings booked, and Breakout was handling conversations that used to take hours of rep time."_ ( [Vikas Aditya, CEO, HackerEarth](https://getbreakout.ai/customers/hackerearth))

### **FAQ**

#### **Is Salesloft still a standalone sales engagement platform?**

Not in the way it used to be. Salesloft merged with Clari in December 2025, and product development since then has centered on unifying Salesloft's engagement and conversation data with Clari's forecasting engine under a single "Predictive Revenue System." Engagement features are still there, but the roadmap priority has shifted toward forecasting and revenue orchestration.

#### **Does Breakout replace Outreach or Salesloft?**

No, and we wouldn't pitch it that way. Breakout sits upstream of both, engaging and qualifying inbound website visitors before they become a lead in someone's sequence. Most of our customers run Breakout alongside an outbound platform like Outreach or Salesloft, not instead of one.

#### **Which one should I pick if I'm choosing between Outreach and Salesloft right now?**

It depends on what you're actually solving for. Pick Outreach if consistent deal execution across a large rep team is your bottleneck. Pick Salesloft if forecast accuracy matters more and you're comfortable being an early customer on an integration still in progress, and confirm renewal terms and roadmap commitments before signing.

#### **Does Breakout work regardless of which one, Outreach or Salesloft, I choose?**

Yes. Breakout runs on your website independently of whatever outbound platform sits underneath it, and Spoc connects to either one, both, or neither. The Outreach-versus-Salesloft decision doesn't gate anything about how Breakout functions.

#### **Is Breakout actually cheaper than Outreach or Salesloft?**

It depends on team size, since the pricing models aren't structured the same way. Outreach and Salesloft charge per seat, so a 10-rep team lands around $1,000–1,650/month on either platform. Breakout's Growth plan is a flat $500 for the base plan, and $2,000/month for the Growth plan, regardless of headcount, so it's worth budgeting as an addition to your stack rather than a cheaper substitute for either.
